newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil up on good bunker demand, tight avails.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil up on good bunker demand, tight avails.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barge prices rose early on Thursday on continued good bunker demand and tight prompt supply, reflected by higher August swaps.

Physical high sulphur barges traded at $96, $96.25, $95.50 and $97 fob ARA, with a major buying at the highest number, compared with Wedenesday's highest deals at $96.25. Front month swaps were up 50 cents to $1.

"The market is stronger and this is a reflection of continuous good bunker demand, again today it was up at about 30,000 tonnes. The market is also firmer on firmness everywhere, Singapore, New York," a trader said.
"Everyday this week the market moves up by 50 cents or more. I think there's a bit of a shortage," a second trader said.
Few traders however saw the higher prices as an attempt by the major to bid up the market.
High sulphur fuel cargoes were steady to a touch firmer on the cracked front, with Russian material talked in the $92/$95 mark, traders said. Few cargoes were on offer.
"There's still a big gap there between buyers and sellers. I don't see any non-Russian on offer this morning," the trader added.

Russian high sulphur straight-run was also largely steady with one or two E-4 offered at three means +$2.5 and with buyers at $1 over the quote. No M-100 was seen on offer early in the day, traders said.
